headline: Revenue growth accelerates, losses widen, guidance raised
summary_short: Natera's Q1 2026 revenue rose 38.8% y/y to $696.6M on 18.5% test-volume growth (54.4% in oncology), while the GAAP net loss widened to $85.1M ($0.60/share) from $66.9M a year ago; management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $2.74-2.82B from $2.62-2.70B.
summary_long: Revenue grew 38.8% y/y to $696.6M as volume rose 18.5% (test volumes topped 1M for the first time) and average selling prices improved; oncology volume grew 54.4%. Gross margin expanded to 64.7% from 63.1% on higher revenue and lower per-test costs. Operating expenses rose 36.0% to $538.6M on headcount growth and higher clinical-trial spend, widening the operating loss to $93.5M from $79.2M y/y. Net loss widened to $85.1M ($0.60/share) from $66.9M ($0.50/share) a year ago. Cash was $1,087.9M, up from $1,076.1M at year-end, on $40.2M of operating cash flow. Natera raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $2.74-2.82B from $2.62-2.70B, and gave gross margin guidance of 64-66%.

drivers.explanation: CEO Chapman called it an outstanding quarter with record volume (over one million units for the first time) and strong Signatera/Fetal Focus adoption from 2025 data readouts, prompting a raised full-year revenue outlook.
Growth was driven by an increase in test volume (+18.5% y/y, led by 54.4% oncology growth) and average selling price improvements.
Margin expansion to 64.7% from 63.1% reflects higher revenue and continued progress reducing per-test cost of revenues.
Operating expenses rose 36.0% to $538.6M on headcount growth to support new products and higher clinical-trial spend, outpacing revenue growth.
Net loss widened as $538.6M of opex (+36.0%) plus new $5.7M intangible amortization outweighed the $134.1M y/y gross-profit gain.
Cash rose $11.8M q/q on $40.2M operating cash flow and $3.7M financing inflow, partly offset by $32.1M of capex plus a related-party investment.
Equity rose as additional paid-in capital grew $146.6M (stock issuance/compensation), more than offsetting the $85.1M net loss added to accumulated deficit.
